heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium image generation, cinematic video, and multimodal creative control.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed autoplay hero video with a dark overlay and orange-tinted control chips, then layer a compact right-side model card stack over the motion field. Keep the layout intentionally asymmetrical and operational-dashboard in feel: logo proof strip near the top, bold H1 at 64px minimum, concise supporting copy, and a primary orange CTA with a secondary outline CTA. Add subtle grid lines, soft gradient mesh, and one or two floating data chips to create premium motion without clutter.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a full-bleed video hero, then switch immediately to a compact logo trust bar
Use a process-led how-it-works section before detailed product blocks to satisfy warm traffic intent
Alternate product storytelling modes between split-panel and spotlight-plus-grid so adjacent sections never feel duplicated
Move from logos to process to proof to features, then close with pricing and a final CTA-led conversion block
Use one visually expressive dark section in the hero, then return to lighter operational panels for readability
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation for Creative Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore the workflow, see logo proof, compare capabilities, and get started.

sections.backgroundTreatment: full-bleed motion background with dark overlay, orange control chips, and compact logo trust strip below the CTA
sections.designNote: Hero must answer what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep it content-first over motion, but visually premium. Headline should stay close to the ad message: AI image and video generation with ByteDance models for creative professionals. CTA is singular and must read 'Get started' in accent orange, full-width on mobile.

Logo-first trust is essential. Use a compact 3-6 logo grid if recognisable logos are available; if not, replace with a minimal metric strip. Keep this visually lightweight and immediately after the hero to reinforce credibility without slowing the warm-traffic flow.

Insert a concise 3-step process section under 60 seconds, because warm visitors want fast clarity before deep proof. Use three numbered cards with one visual strip or small timeline preview. Keep copy short and operational: prompt/input, generate, refine/export. Use a lighter, cleaner surface than the hero to create contrast.

Use proof immediately after the process. If logo assets are strong, show a static flex-wrap logo grid with recognizable brand marks; otherwise use a metric strip. This section should feel credible and compact, not testimonial-heavy. Keep the tone industry-appropriate and polished.

Because there are two product sections and each has 5+ features, do not use a static card grid. Use alternating product blocks: first product as visual-first split panel, second product as a different energy pattern, either tabs-with-preview or accordion-with-visual. Seedream 4.5 should spotlight 1-2 differentiating capabilities first: high-resolution image quality and precise text rendering / multi-image composition. Seedance 1.5 Pro should shift to cinematic motion, audio-video sync, and speed. Keep adjacent product blocks structurally different so the page feels designed, not templated.

Use a two-card comparison with one highlighted option, but keep it clean and editorial rather than salesy. Since the user intent is evaluation, the pricing block should clarify what each model is for and make the 'Get started' CTA the dominant action. Avoid gray or outlined buttons.

There are 4+ testimonials, so use a grid or a static carousel. Prefer a 3-card first row with a subtle fourth card or expandable carousel on smaller screens. Keep quotes from creative roles prominent and concise, emphasizing turnaround time, precision, and synchronized audio-video output.

End with a conversion-led but not aggressive lead capture block. Because CTA aggression is moderate and the warm-traffic sequence prefers 'See it in action' over hard signup language, the form should still use only the button text 'Get started'. Make the card centered, clean, and high contrast with orange accent fill.

blueprint.designPersonality: A premium enterprise creative platform with dashboard clarity, motion-led depth, and logo-dominant trust. It should feel like an AI production console for serious teams: structured, fast, polished, and unmistakably branded to Techjockey's orange identity.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a cinematic AI-generated background video of abstract creative workflows, prompt-to-visual transformations, timeline motion, and generated imagery overlays. Support with SVG logo rows for trust, PNG model cards for Seedream and Seedance, and clean dashboard-like metric chips that communicate quality, speed, and multimodal control.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and needs a compact, high-clarity size to preserve hierarchy without wrapping too aggressively in a motion-led hero.

colours.colourReason: Use Techjockey's brand orange as the dominant identity with white, charcoal, and soft grey support. This keeps the page on-brand and distinct while avoiding any invented secondary palette.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top hero with brand/logo at upper left, large centered/left-aligned headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefits list using checkmark bullets. Strong content-first framing with minimal visual clutter and no obvious hero media.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column vertical flow with a prominent hero, then a conversion section/form card immediately below. Content is organized into stacked modules with clear hierarchy rather than complex multi-column storytelling.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primary reusable card is a simple bordered/boxed form card with strong title, internal fields, and utility spacing. Overall card language is functional rather than decorative, with minimal shadow treatment implied and emphasis on readability.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears as a high-visibility action tied to lead generation or demo request. Secondary CTA is absent, indicating a single-action conversion pattern. CTA placement is concentrated in the hero or adjacent conversion module rather than repeated throughout.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module visible in the reference structure. If reused, pricing should be added as a separate mid-to-late page section with simple plan cards, but this page itself does not establish a pricing pattern.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not shown; likely minimal or standard utility footer outside the visible pattern. No evidence of heavy footer content blocks or sitemap-style density.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Light media usage with brand logo only in the hero. No hero image, product mockup, or embedded video is present in the extracted structure. Visual communication relies on typography and list structure rather than media panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Product content is best expressed as stacked feature modules, each with a label, headline, short description, and bullet-like feature list. The reference favors clear segmentation by product name/category, with each module acting like a mini landing section.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead capture form directly follows the hero in a dedicated card. Pattern uses hidden tracking fields plus visible form inputs, indicating a conversion-focused, qualification-oriented workflow. Form is presented as a separate block rather than an inline hero form.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, non-animated presentation with no visible motion systems. Interaction emphasis is on form submission rather than navigation effects or micro-interactions.
designNotes: Conversion-first layout with immediate qualification form after hero.
Use concise feature bullets and short descriptive copy blocks.
Prefer one primary action per section to reduce friction.
Maintain generous whitespace and clear section separation.
If expanded for this product, use the same modular layout for image and video offerings to keep symmetry.

avoidPatterns: Do not use a grid inside a grid for the feature section
Do not make the page hero-only; the full page must be visible and scrollable immediately
Do not leave empty black space in the layout
Do not add a form unless the page explicitly requires one
Do not place media on the right side of the hero when no form is present

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is aimed at professionals evaluating advanced AI creative tools, so the strongest conversion path is a demo-booking journey rather than instant purchase. The audience is solution-aware and will respond best to a product-led story that clearly separates the two models while showing practical creative benefits. Since the instruction says visitors trust logos most, trust must be led by a sticky logo strip rather than testimonials or badges. The hero should be immersive with video background to match the product category and create immediate visual relevance, but the content needs to stay message-first so the value proposition is instantly clear. The page should feel premium and efficient, with balanced density to keep technical credibility without overwhelming the reader. Strong CTAs are appropriate because the offer is a demo/quote motion for a high-consideration AI product.
